correctness.rationale: The projective action is faithful by the three-point test; the order of PGL2 is the full permutation order at q=2,3. Swapping an inversion sends both ratios inside the original interval [b_k/a_j,b_l/a_i] for i<j and k<l; adjacent swaps terminate, including when weights tie. For i<j both r_j/r_i and its reciprocal are at most n, and equality in the chain of bounds requires exactly the stated repeated weight and 1,n endpoints. The kernel-column construction gives weights equal to nonzero length minus the kernel multiplicity, has rank two with at least two distinct represented kernels, and gives both sharp examples for every n≥3 with the specified zero padding. For n=2 the only rank-two code is the whole space. At q=4 the translations, nonzero dilations and inversion act evenly and generate a group of order 60; the odd transposition is the only weight-preserving matching. Every feasible matching has product of ratios 1 and is not constant, so it has an upward ratio at least 10/9 and a downward one at most 9/10. The identity attains both. The algorithm examines a constant number of messages and candidate projective maps and hence is linear in block length over either fixed field.
